findings.current: If the greatest archer under Heaven hadn’t helped him—a man who could tear apart a target from hundreds of jang away—even the Slaughter Saint would never have made it back in one piece.
findings.defect: The appositive calls the Bow Saint a man, contradicting the established she/her decision and her pronouns later in the chapter.
findings.rationale: Keeps the action and description intact while correcting the character reference.
findings.replacement: If the greatest archer under Heaven hadn’t helped him—a woman who could tear apart a target from hundreds of jang away—even the Slaughter Saint would never have made it back in one piece.
findings.source: Chapter 1115, Slaughter Saint’s recollection of the fight with the Black Ghosts

findings.current: An enemy army estimated at no less than thirty thousand had finally appeared here, today.
findings.defect: “Appeared here” suggests the army is at the East Gate, though the defenders cannot see it; Chapter 1119 places the horn several hundred jang away, and the active state says the coalition has not been shown reaching the gate.
findings.rationale: Preserves the defenders’ inference from the horn without presenting the army as visibly present or already at the gate.
findings.replacement: An enemy army estimated at no less than thirty thousand had finally drawn near.
findings.source: Chapter 1118, defenders hearing the horn east of the gate

summary: One clear pronoun error and one arrival claim that conflicts with the reading copy and active state.
